distribution: Recorded only from Lanyu Island, Taiwan.
soldier: The head capsule is brown tinged with yellow; the mandibles dark brown, almost black, the mandibular bases concolorous with the head capsule; the labrum, antennae, frontal gland pore and compound eyes yellowish brown; the thorax, abdomen and legs also yellowish brown. The whole body is sparsely covered with hairs; the periphery of the pronotum bears only scattered bristles, with two visible in the middle region. The head capsule is broadly elliptical, the sides expanding backwards from the mandibular bases and becoming almost parallel behind the compound eyes, the posterior margin broadly rounded, the widest point near the middle. The labrum is nearly square, its apex flat and slightly concave, with two apical hairs directed forwards; the anteclypeus is a transverse band, the postclypeus trapezoidal. The mandibles are sabre-like, their apices slender and slightly curved, the base with a distinct mandibular condyle, the middle of the inner margin almost smooth. Antennae with 17 segments, segments 3 and 4 both rather short. The compound eyes are distinct and slightly bulging. The frontal gland pore is circular and lies behind two-fifths of the anterior part of the head capsule, with a shallow groove in front of the pore leading to the clypeus, the groove slightly wider than the pore, the area around the pore slightly depressed and bearing several fine forward-curving arcs; in lateral view the surface in front of and behind the pore is rather flat, and the dorsal margin of the head runs straight backwards from the clypeus. The broad region of the postmentum lies at one-quarter of the anterior part, the middle of its anterolateral margin slightly concave inwards, the surface of the broad region slightly arched and bearing several arc lines; the waist lies at one-third of the posterior part of the postmentum, the length of the postmentum about six times the width of the waist. The pronotum is kidney-shaped, with a broad V-shaped shallow notch in the middle of the anterior margin, the lateral and posterior margins continuous in a broad arc, the margin of the disc slightly upturned and most evidently so at the sides; the mesonotum and metanotum are both about as broad as the pronotum.
taxonomy_note: Recorded in the original work as Prorhinotermes japonicus, now merged as a synonym into P. flavus.
